is_anopheles.evidence: The study evaluated efficacy against Anopheles gambiae sensu stricto (Kisumu and Muleba-Kis strains; page 1, 6-7).

reports_target_markers.evidence: No genotyping was performed in this study. The authors only mention that the colonized Muleba-Kis strain has 'fixed L1014S kdr frequency' citing previous literature (page 6-7).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No genotype counts, allele counts, or frequencies with sample sizes were generated or reported in this paper.

african_field_population.evidence: The study exclusively tested laboratory colonies: susceptible An. gambiae s.s. Kisumu and pyrethroid-resistant An. gambiae s.s. Muleba-Kis colonized for over 8 years, used in bioassays and experimental hut release-recapture experiments (page 6-8).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary research study evaluating the laboratory and semi-field efficacy of permethrin-PBO treated blankets.

sub_country_location.evidence: The experimental hut trial was conducted at Harusini, Mabogini village (S03˚22.764' E03˚720.793'), Lower Moshi, Tanzania (page 6).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Experimental hut release-recapture trials were conducted from June to August 2021 (page 8).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Standard experimental hut trial evaluating treated blankets using laboratory colonies.

supplement.evidence: No supplementary data is needed; the paper is inherently ineligible due to lack of genotyping and lack of field-collected mosquito populations.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated the efficacy of permethrin-PBO treated blankets against pyrethroid-susceptible (Kisumu) and pyrethroid-resistant (Muleba-Kis) laboratory strains of Anopheles gambiae s.s. using WHO cylinder assays, tunnel tests, and experimental hut release-recapture trials in Lower Moshi, Tanzania. No field populations were collected and no marker genotyping was performed.
exclusion_reasons: No target resistance markers were genotyped in this study.
Only colonized laboratory strains (Kisumu and Muleba-Kis) were tested; no African field populations were sampled.
